sections.title: Introduction & Core Philosophy
sections.summary: OryxOps is the flagship operations platform for Qatari Virtual — combining pilot-driven scheduling, virtual economics, Infinite Flight Live persistence, and a full Electronic Flight Bag suite.
sections.content:
Welcome to **OryxOps**, the flagship operations platform designed exclusively for **Qatari Virtual**.

In traditional management systems where staff face the tedious task of manually creating dozens of flight schedules per day, OryxOps completely reinvents this workflow:

### Core Pillars
- **Pilot-Driven Scheduling**: Pilots propose the exact routes they wish to fly within structured airline boundaries.
- **Economic Progression**: Earn virtual currency (QAR) on every flight to spend within the airline ecosystem.
- **Persistent World Engine**: Integrated directly with Infinite Flight Live — aircraft stay where they are parked.
- **Advanced EFB Suite**: Audio co-pilots, wind analyzers, interactive checklists, and real-time dispatch systems.

### How the System Works
1. You propose a flight on the Schedule Calendar (costs a proposal token).
2. Management approves or rejects the proposal.
3. You (or another pilot) book the approved flight.
4. You dispatch, fly, and file your PIREP to earn QAR.
5. QAR feeds back into buying more proposal tokens — creating a self-sustaining economy.

sections.title: Infinite Flight Live & Persistence
sections.summary: OryxOps is built on Infinite Flight's persistent fleet model — aircraft physically stay at their last parked airport until another pilot repositions them.
sections.content:
OryxOps operates on top of Infinite Flight's **persistent fleet model (IF Live)**. Unlike standard free-flight modes where an aircraft can be spawned anywhere, Live introduces physical persistence.

### Key Concept: Location Continuity
If an aircraft lands at London Heathrow (EGLL), it stays parked at EGLL until another pilot flies or repositions it. This is why the Schedule Calendar always shows the aircraft's **current airport** — that's where your next flight must depart from.

### Fleet Status
- **Visible** — Aircraft is on the ramp and can be spawned.
- **Hangared** — Aircraft is stored and temporarily unavailable.
- **Parked / Flying / Maintenance** — Internal OryxOps status shown on Fleet Registry cards.

### Active vs. Stored Fleet
The active fleet size is bounded by the organization's Level (boosted by member Lifts). Active slots determine which aircraft can be assigned active schedules.

sections.title: The Dashboard — Your Home Base
sections.summary: Your personal command center — shows your wallet balance, active booking, weekly proposal usage, airline-wide metrics, and quick action shortcuts.
sections.content:
The **Dashboard** is the first page you see after login and your primary command center.

### Hero Banner (Top)
- **Live UTC Zulu Clock** — updates every second.
- Time-based greeting (Good Morning / Afternoon / Evening).
- Your **Pilot Title**, **Name**, and **Callsign** badge.
- Your **Pilot Wallet** (QAR balance) in the top-right corner.

### Active Flight Alert
- **Blue banner** appears if you have an active booking — shows flight number, route (e.g. OTHH → EGLL), aircraft registration, and a direct **Open EFB** button.
- If no active booking: a prompt to **Browse Schedule** is shown instead.

### Stat Cards
- **Weekly Proposals** — shows used / total with a progress bar (turns red at ≥80%). Links to Shop.
- **Pilot Wallet** — your QAR balance plus short-haul and long-haul token stockpiles.

### Airline Operations Strip (Dark Panel)
- **Global Airline Rating** — average reputation score (0–5 stars) across all pilots' completed flights.
- **Completed Flights** — total revenue legs filed across all pilots since the airline launched.

### Proposal Transaction Log
- Shows the last 8 token purchase and consumption events.
- Each entry shows description, flight detail (if applicable), and cost.

### Quick Actions Grid
- 4 shortcut tiles: **Fleet**, **Schedule**, **Operations**, and **EFB**.

sections.title: Schedule Calendar — Propose & Book Flights
sections.summary: The heart of OryxOps. Propose flights, get them approved, and book them here. Flight cards progress through Draft → Proposed → Approved before you can book and fly.
sections.content:
The **Schedule Calendar** is the core of OryxOps. All flight proposals, approvals, and bookings happen here. It shows one week at a time.

### Calendar Views
- **Calendar View** — a 7-day × 24-hour UTC grid. Click any empty cell to create a flight.
- **List View** — a sorted list of all flights for the week.

### Flight Status Colours
- 🔵 **Draft** — Created but not submitted for review.
- 🟡 **Proposed** — Submitted, awaiting management approval.
- 🟢 **Approved** — Available to book and fly.
- 🔴 **Cancelled** — Flight cancelled.

### Step 1 — Create a Draft
1. Go to Schedule page.
2. Click Add flight on date which you want to schedule your flight.
3. Select your **aircraft** (loaded from the active fleet).
4. Select a **route** (automatically loaded from the aircraft's current parked airport and type).
5. Set the **departure time** (UTC) and **ground time** (turnaround minutes).
6. Click **Save** — card appears as Draft (blue).

### Step 2 — Propose the Flight
1. Click the Draft card.
2. Click **Propose Flight**.
3. Consumes 1 proposal token (free weekly allowance or a purchased token if you've exceeded your limit).

### 🎟️ What is a Proposal Token?

A **Proposal Token** is a token used in OryxOps that allows pilots to request and schedule custom flight routes for active fleet aircraft.

Instead of waiting for management staff to manually assign flights, pilots use Proposal Tokens to convert draft routes into official flight proposals for Admin review.

### ❓ Why is it there?

The Proposal Token system was created for two main operational reasons:

1. **Prevents Schedule Overcrowding & Spam:** Without tokens, pilots could generate unlimited schedules on aircraft, blocking other pilots from using fleet airframes or creating operational chaos.
2. **Promotes Pilot Progression & Realism:** It reflects airline resource management. Captains are given more scheduling authority than First Officers, encouraging pilots to rank up.

### ⚙️ How does it work & What is its Usage?

* **Submitting a Flight Proposal:** When you create a draft flight on the Schedule Calendar, tapping **Propose Flight** consumes **1 Proposal Token**. The flight then moves to management for approval.

* **Weekly Free Limits:** Every pilot receives a weekly free allowance of proposal tokens based on rank:
* 🧑‍✈️ **First Officers:** 3 Free Proposals per week
* 👨‍✈️ **Captains:** 6 Free Proposals per week

* **The Proposal Shop (Extra Slots):** If you run out of free weekly tokens and want to propose more flights, you can buy additional tokens from the Proposal Shop using your earned QAR balance:


* ✈️ **Short-Haul Token (<8hrs):** Costs **1,000 QAR**
* 🌐 **Long-Haul Token (>8hrs):** Costs **2,000 QAR**

> 🛡️ **Refund Guarantee:** If management rejects your proposed flight, your consumed token or paid QAR fee is automatically refunded back to your account!

4. Once Proposal Token consumed, Card will turn yellow (Proposed) and queues for management review.

### Step 3 — Management Approval
- **Approved** → card turns green, available to book.
- **Rejected** → card cancelled; your token is automatically refunded.

### Step 4 — Book the Flight
1. Click an approved (green) flight card.
2. Choose your booking type:
- **Departure Only** — fly takeoff through top of cruise.
- **Arrival Only** — Spawn ETA ~30 mins ETA and fly approach & landing.
- **Both Parts (Full Flight)** — fly the entire leg.
3. Click **Book** — confirmed!

### Warnings
- **Position Mismatch Warning** — Red warning if a flight departs from a different airport than where the aircraft will actually be based on prior scheduled arrivals.
- **Ground Time Warning** — Orange warning if the gap between consecutive flights is shorter than the required turnaround time.

sections.title: The Shop — Proposal Tokens
sections.summary: Spend earned QAR to pre-purchase extra proposal tokens for flights beyond your weekly free allowance. Tokens are only consumed if management approves your proposal.
sections.content:
The **Shop** is where you spend your earned QAR to pre-purchase extra proposal tokens beyond your weekly free allowance.

### Token Products
- **Short-Haul Proposal Token** — For flights under 8 hours. Costs **1,000 QAR**.
- **Long-Haul Proposal Token** — For flights 8 hours or more. Costs **2,000 QAR**.

### How Tokens Work
1. Purchase tokens in the Shop using your QAR balance.
2. Tokens are stored in your account (visible on Dashboard and Shop page).
3. When you propose a flight **beyond your free weekly limit**, the system automatically uses a stored token instead of charging your wallet directly.
4. Tokens are consumed only if management **approves** your proposal.
5. If your proposal is **rejected** → token is automatically refunded.

### Insufficient Funds
The Buy button is disabled and labelled **Insufficient Funds** if your wallet balance is below the token cost.

### Where to See Your Token Balance
- **Dashboard** → Pilot Wallet stat card (shows short-haul and long-haul token counts).
- **Shop page** → Your Proposal Tokens panel.

sections.title: Flight Operations — Dispatch, Fuel & PIREP
sections.summary: Manage everything after booking — dispatch the flight, generate your SimBrief plan, calculate fuel, and file your PIREP to earn QAR and update the airline rating.
sections.content:
**Flight Operations** is where you manage everything after booking and before / during the actual flight. You must have an active booking to access most tools.

### Active Booking Overview Card
Displays your current booked flight: route, flight number, aircraft, crew layout (Solo or Split Crew), pax count, and status (Pre-flight or Dispatched).

### Step 1 — Dispatch the Flight (Departure Pilot Only)
Click **🚀 Dispatch Flight** to:
- Generate a dynamic **passenger manifest** (pax count) based on the airline's Global Reputation rating.
- Unlock all active operations tools.
- Trigger an animated **Passenger Boarding Modal**.

### Step 2 — Plan Your Flight
- **🔗 Generate SimBrief Dispatch Plan** — Opens SimBrief with your route, pax, aircraft, and flight number pre-filled.
- **📡 Fleet Movement Broadcast** — Click **Send Webhook Status** to post a live enroute status ping to the #fleet-logs Discord channel.

### Step 3 — Calculate Fuel
Enter your flight duration (hours + minutes). The estimator calculates fuel burn using aircraft-specific hourly rates:
- A321: 2,700 kg/hr
- A330 / A333: 5,500 kg/hr
- A359 / A35K: 5,800 kg/hr
- A388: 11,500 kg/hr
- B77W / B77L: 6,800 kg/hr

Click **Copy to PIREP** to auto-fill the PIREP fuel field.

### Step 4 — File PIREP (Arrival Pilot Only)
After landing, fill in:
- **Flight Duration** (actual HH:MM)
- **Fuel Burned** (kg)
- **Landing Smoothness** (FPM — feet per minute)
- **Flight Diverted?** — toggle ON if you landed at an alternate airport
- **Actual Landing Airport** (ICAO) — only shown if diverted

Click **✅ File PIREP & Finish Leg** to submit and earn your QAR.

### The Airline Economic Flywheel
High pilot performance → increases Global Airline Rating → boosts passenger demand → increases QAR earnings for all pilots.

sections.title: Electronic Flight Bag (EFB)
sections.summary: Your full in-flight cockpit tablet with 6 tabs: Briefing, Checklist (voice co-pilot), Weather, Aircraft performance, Charts, and Settings.
sections.content:
The **EFB** is your full in-flight cockpit tablet with 6 tabs. It requires an active booking and auto-loads SimBrief OFP data if your SimBrief Pilot ID is configured in Settings.

### Tab 1 — Briefing
Shows route, ETD, ETA, cruise altitude, fuel, payload, SID/STAR procedures, and an embedded SimBrief PDF viewer. Toggle between SimBrief data and your booking data as the source.

### Tab 2 — Checklist (Voice Co-Pilot)
A fully dynamic interactive checklist. Values are calculated from your aircraft type, payload percentage, and flight direction.

**Checklist Phases**: PRE-FLIGHT NOTAMS → ENGINE START → BEFORE TAXI → BEFORE TAKEOFF → TAKEOFF → CLIMB → CRUISE → DESCENT → APPROACH → AFTER LANDING → SHUTDOWN

**Co-Pilot Modes**:
- **Manual** — Tap each item to check it off.
- **Voice** — Say the trigger keyword (default: "check") → co-pilot reads the item → speak the response → fuzzy matching validates your answer.
- **Keyboard** — Use a configured key (default: Space) to advance items.


### Tab 3 — Weather
- **Decoded METAR** for departure and arrival airports.
- **3-Step METAR Timeline** — shows how weather evolves across Infinite Flight's weather cycle.
- **Runway Wind Vector** — enter runway heading to get exact headwind/crosswind components.
- **Automated Diversion Finder** — searches nearby eligible alternate airports if destination weather is poor.

### Tab 4 — Aircraft Performance
- Engine start sequence (correct order per aircraft type).
- Engine stable N1/N2 percentage.
- Flap retraction and deployment speed schedules.
- Step climb advisor (recommends altitude changes during cruise for fuel efficiency).
- Landing data table (approach speeds by load %).


### Tab 5 — Charts
ChartFox airport charts embedded directly in the EFB. Search any airport by ICAO code and browse SID, STAR, approach, and airport diagram charts without leaving the Web.

### Tab 6 — Settings
Configure co-pilot voice, speech rate, pitch, trigger keyword, input mode, chime sounds, auto-advance, and checklist overrides (aircraft type, load %, flight direction).

sections.title: Fleet Registry
sections.summary: Browse all official aircraft in Qatar Virtual's fleet. See live IF status, current airport, flight hours, and assigned pilots.
sections.content:
The **Fleet Registry** displays all official active aircraft in Qatari Virtual's fleet.

### Aircraft Card Shows
- **Registration** (e.g., A7-ALR, A7-ANG, A7-BAE)
- **Aircraft type & livery** (e.g., Airbus A350-900, Boeing 777-300ER)
- **Status badge** — Parked (green) / Flying (blue) / Maintenance (amber)
- **IF Live badge** — if the airframe is linked to Infinite Flight Live
- **IF Visibility** — Visible (on ramp) or Hangared
- **Current Airport** (e.g., 📍 OTHH)
- **Total Flight Hours** (e.g., 🕐 142h)
- **Total Legs Flown** (e.g., ✈ 38 legs)
- **Current Pilot** (if a pilot is currently assigned)

### Click Any Aircraft
Opens the detailed airframe profile showing full metadata and complete flight history.

sections.title: Pilot Promotion
sections.summary: Fleet progression and promotion mechanics in OryxOps.
sections.content:
## Fleet Progression (Work in Progress)

> **Note:** The fleet progression and rank system is currently **under development**. The information below outlines our **current vision** for how the system will work. As development continues, features, requirements, and mechanics may change based on testing and community feedback.

### Planned Fleet Progression

Traditional VA systems automatically unlock larger aircraft after reaching a certain number of hours, despite having limited physical frames and pilot slots. If aircraft progression is purely based on hours, eventually 70–80% of active pilots could grind their way into the highest ranks.

OryxOps aims to simulate how fleet progression works in real-world airlines.

Each aircraft type has a **limited number of pilot slots**, representing the airline's available crew positions. Because these slots are finite, access to higher aircraft will not be granted automatically.

Instead, progression is planned to work through a **Vacancy & Bidding System**.

When a position becomes available—such as when the fleet receives a new aircraft or a pilot transfers to another fleet—a bidding process will open. Eligible pilots may submit their application for the vacant position.

Management will then review all applicants using factors such as:

* Total flight experience
* Seniority
* Activity and performance
* Current aircraft rating
* Other operational requirements

The selected pilot will transfer to the new fleet, creating a vacancy in their previous aircraft assignment. This vacancy can then be filled through another bidding process, allowing progression to naturally flow throughout the fleet.

This system is designed to:

* Keep fleet progression realistic.
* Maintain the value of higher aircraft.
* Prevent overcrowding on limited fleets.
* Create meaningful progression beyond simply accumulating flight hours.

While flight hours and experience will remain important, they are planned to determine a pilot's **eligibility and competitiveness** for available positions rather than automatically unlocking new aircraft.

**Please remember:** This system is still under active development, and all mechanics described above are subject to change before release.
